summary.headline: Laxmi Dental Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR79.5 crore (up ~10% YoY from INR72.3 crore), with EBITDA up 38.5% to INR15.3 crore and margin at 19.2%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 set record quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with gross margin up to 76.9% from 68.5% on product mix, and PAT up 17.6% to INR10 crore. Dental lab, aligner and pediatric segments all grew, and domestic lab digital penetration reached about 78%. Scanner sales fell sharply to INR3.5 crore from INR8.9 crore, and management launched a scanner subscription model about three weeks before the call. H1 FY27 revenue was INR154.2 crore, and the company stays debt-free with about INR97 crore in cash and investments.

segments.name: Dental lab (total)
segments.commentary: Grew 22.7% YoY; international lab up about 32% and domestic lab up about 15%. Domestic digital penetration is about 78% against a medium-term target of over 90%. Domestic lab and international lab both reported their highest-ever quarterly revenue.

segments.name: Aligner solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 23.5% YoY. Bizdent (branded clear aligner, Illusion) grew 27.7% and Vedia grew 19.1%. Management cited B2C aligner revenue of INR13.2 crore against B2B raw material sales of INR11.5 crore, mostly international.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (pediatric)
segments.commentary: Grew 16.7% YoY. Management said H1 JV profit share fell about 35% because the entity moved from a tax-holiday start-up benefit to regular tax; it denied any one-off or margin contraction.

segments.name: Scanners
segments.commentary: Scanner sales were INR3.5 crore in Q2 FY27 against INR8.9 crore a year earlier. Management said about 215 scanners were sold in the first ~6 months of FY27, against a run rate of about 250 per quarter last year.

guidance_outlook: Domestic lab digital penetration to reach over 90% in the medium term; management earlier cited a 90-95% goal.
Tariff refund of about INR5.5 crore (excluding interest) to be reflected in Q3 FY27 results.
IPO proceeds of INR48.1 crore unutilised; now to go to owned manufacturing (above INR27 crore for land and buildings, above INR21 crore for machinery and equipment), deployed across FY27 and FY28.

New self-owned horizontal integrated facility to replace leased Mira Road plants; transition to be completed by end of FY2028. Planned site size of 1.25-1.5 lakh sq ft against current 35,000-40,000 sq ft, though land is not yet acquired.
Management expects gross margin to move from about 77% to 78-80% over time, with most margin gains coming from people and process efficiency.
Management plans a semi-automated lab in the US and is evaluating labs in other countries; no timeline given.

Subscription scanner model: INR50,000 deposit plus INR3,000 + GST per month, with a commitment of INR25,000 business per month by the dentist. Management said the campaign is about three weeks old and it has a few thousand leads.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex was about INR16.7 crore; IPO proceeds to fund the owned facility build-out across FY27 and FY28.
Management said it can expand aligner capacity quickly in India; the planned overseas labs are part of the mid-to-long-term strategy, with no capacity figures disclosed.
The new Indian facility will serve only the company's own brand (Illusion); management ruled out white-labelling.
Company manufactures all aligner components in-house, including sheets, from a 50,000 sq ft facility.
demand_pricing: Clinics make up the majority of customers; hospitals are under 1%. The company does not sell through pharmacies.
Payment terms are typically 30-60 days on monthly invoicing, both domestic and international.
International sales span 90-100 countries, mainly by air. Constant-currency international growth was given as about 8-10% YoY, a range management would not confirm as constant.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 aligner demand is supported by pay-as-you-go phased delivery and brand campaigns featuring Kareena as brand ambassador.
Management said that in the scanner subscription model a dentist's laptop cost has risen from about INR1 lakh to about INR2 lakh, lifting total cost of entry to about INR5.2-5.4 lakh.
Hub-and-spoke model is raising wallet share per dentist. Management said domestic growth went from single digits last quarter to 15% this quarter.
Management views aligner competition as likely to consolidate to 3-4 leading players within 2-5 years and said trust in the brand is its edge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the constant-currency growth of international business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said roughly 8-10% YoY, depending on monthly realisations, but would not confirm it was constant-currency; an analyst asked for a consistent constant-currency disclosure going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What are the gross margin drivers and trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin excluding scanners was 76.9% in Q2, in a historical range of 75-77%. Management said it rose both QoQ and YoY; it sees upside to 78-80% through people and process efficiency rather than to 85-90%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics and scale of the subscription scanner model?
qa_highlights.answer: Dentist pays INR50,000 deposit plus INR3,000 + GST monthly, with a INR25,000 monthly business commitment. Management said about 14 scanners sold in the first 2.5 weeks, and that 1,000 deployed scanners would add about INR2.5 crore of monthly business.

qa_highlights.question: Can scanners move between dentists, and would competitors copy the model?
qa_highlights.answer: Scanners stay with the dentist while business commitments are met; after two months of shortfall they are reclaimed and redeployed. No competitor has been observed; management said the model needs substantial tech and subscription management skills.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Kids-e-Dental JV profit share fall about 35% in H1 despite 33% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-off and no margin contraction; the entity's start-up tax benefit ended after three years, so it now pays regular tax.

qa_highlights.question: What are the planned overseas and new Indian lab plans and their economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Overseas labs will be hybrid, with digital work in India and semi-automated and CNC or 3D printing in-country; the US lab is planned because a US CEO has been appointed. The new Indian plant is 1.25-1.5 lakh sq ft, with land not yet acquired.

risks_watch: Scanner sales fell to INR3.5 crore from INR8.9 crore YoY. The subscription model's uptake and the cash-flow cost of scanners kept on the balance sheet are not yet visible.
Laptop prices roughly doubled and raised dentist cost of entry, slowing digital adoption. Management said deployments are being held until after Diwali.
Aligner competition is intensifying, with funded entrants. Management expects consolidation in 2-5 years but gave no market share data.
Kids-e-Dental JV profit share fell about 35% in H1 after the tax holiday ended; watch the effect on consolidated PAT.
The Mira Road plant move and new facility are due by end of FY28, with capex to be funded from the IPO proceeds and the INR97 crore cash balance. Execution timeline and cost are not yet defined.
Management gave no case volumes or realisation data, and no constant-currency figure was confirmed; watch for these next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and margins, with management stressing record revenue and EBITDA. It was guarded on quantifiable items: it declined to give case counts, aligner B2C realisation, a clear constant-currency growth figure and scanner subscription volumes, and said it would revert next quarter.
key_quotes: Our revenue for Q2 FY27 stood at INR79.5 crores, recording a highest-ever quarterly revenue as well as EBITDA.

The scanners deployed with our dental partners over the past few years were meant to deepen our connection with this clinic and create higher recurring opportunities across our laboratory and aligner business.
So we are very clear in our strategy that we are a B2B2C company where we educate the patient, but our last message in every communication is ask your dentist.
